# 🗓️ Brisbane Events Digest — Week of 11–17 May 2026

> Sources checked: Eventbrite, Eventfinda, The Triffid, Fortitude Music Hall, Princess Theatre, Brisbane Powerhouse / Brisbane Comedy Festival, Palace Cinemas (German Film Festival, National Theatre Live), IMA Brisbane, Milani Gallery, Meetup, Visit Brisbane, AllEvents, Ticketek, Songkick, and more. Events outside the 11–17 May window have been excluded.

## 🎭 ARTS / EXHIBITION

---

### 1. 🖼️ Platform 2026 — Dean Ansell, Spencer Harvie & Seren Wagstaff *(ongoing exhibition)*
- **Dates:** Running throughout May 2026 (open Tue–Sun, 10am–5pm)
- **Venue:** Institute of Modern Art (IMA), Ground Floor, Judith Wright Arts Centre, 420 Brunswick St, Fortitude Valley
- **Cost:** Free
- **Category:** Arts / Exhibition
- **Source:** [ima.org.au/exhibitions/platform-2026](https://www.ima.org.au/exhibitions/platform-2026/)

Platform is the IMA's annual Queensland-emerging-artist exhibition. Each year they fund three artists to create ambitious new projects — this year presenting new works by Dean Ansell, Spencer Harvie, and Seren Wagstaff. Spencer Harvie explores dark, surreal, nonsensical aspects of online and fan subcultures, processing AI-generated and imagined imagery within an elaborate cartoon logic. A rich, thought-provoking free gallery show from one of Brisbane's most credible contemporary art institutions.

Platform is the IMA's annual Queensland-emerging-artist exhibition, funding three artists to create ambitious new projects — Dean Ansell, Spencer Harvie, and Seren Wagstaff. ### 4. 🎬 HSBC German Film Festival 2026 — Palace Cinemas James St & Fortitude Valley
- **Dates:** 8 May – 27 May 2026 *(in-window all week)*
- **Venue:** Palace Cinemas James St (Fortitude Valley) & other Palace venues
- **Cost:** Standard cinema pricing (~$18–$22); Movie Club discounts available
- **Category:** Arts / Film
- **Source / Tickets:** [palacecinemas.com.au/festivals](https://www.palacecinemas.com.au/festivals)

This May, the 2026 HSBC German Film Festival presented by Palace, in association with German Films, will showcase the best contemporary German cinema direct from major festivals in Europe, plus a selection from its German-speaking neighbours Austria and Switzerland. Running all week — a great opportunity to catch curated art-house German cinema.

### 5. 🎬 National Theatre Live: *All My Sons* — Palace Cinemas
- **Dates:** From 7 May 2026 *(in-window all week)*
- **Venue:** Palace Cinemas James St, Fortitude Valley
- **Cost:** Standard cinema pricing
- **Category:** Arts / Film / Theatre Screening
- **Source / Tickets:** [palacecinemas.com.au/events/national-theatre-live](https://www.palacecinemas.com.au/events/national-theatre-live)

Bryan Cranston (*Breaking Bad*) and Marianne Jean-Baptiste (*Hard Truths*) feature in a five-star, triumphantly acclaimed new production of Arthur Miller's *All My Sons*, from visionary director Ivo Van Hove. One family, the heart of the American dream — when wartime delivers profits, it comes at a price. Paapa Essiedu, Tom Glynn-Carney, and Hayley Squires also feature in this disturbingly prescient play, filmed live from London's West End.

The 2026 Alliance Française French Film Festival features *Colours of Time* as its opening night film. The Brisbane opening night includes drinks and French nibbles prior to the premiere of Cédric Klapisch's new dramedy. Screenings run throughout the fortnight.

- **Cost:** Ticketed (check Eventbrite for price)

Attendees weave a basketling in a ceremony-style immersive sharing and healing circle. A hands-on, grounded, community-oriented creative workshop in a beautiful outdoor setting.

### 18. 🗣️ Brisbane Social Geeks — Philosophy, Board Games & Intellectual Discussion Meetups
- **Dates:** Multiple sessions this week (check Meetup page for exact days)
- **Venue:** New Farm Library area & Roma Street Parklands, Brisbane
- **Cost:** Free
- **Category:** Social / Meetup
- **Source:** [meetup.com/philosophy-pub-brisbane](https://www.meetup.com/philosophy-pub-brisbane/)

Brisbane Social Geeks is a group for people who want to enlarge their social connections and develop their bodies and minds — events include social pub nights, boardgaming meetups, philosophy group, guided meditations, yoga, and intellectual discussions. Recent sessions have included a philosophy discussion based on *The Dictator's Handbook*, with prompts like "What is power?", "Can anyone get power?", and "How does anyone keep or lose power?" — held at the small building adjacent to New Farm Library.
